clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old woman presented with 1 month of nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, and anosmia. Initial examination revealed a large tissue growth in her left nasal cavity (E001). A CT scan confirmed a large soft tissue mass opacifying the left maxillary, ethmoidal, frontal, and sphenoid sinuses, with no intracranial extension (E002). Debulking surgery was performed, and a frozen section yielded a provisional diagnosis of poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma (E004). However, formal examination of the whole resected specimen, including immunohistochemistry, revealed a heterogeneous mixture of components from all three germ cell layers (mature benign glandular/stromal, immature malignant glandular/stromal), with undifferentiated components showing CD-99 or synaptophysin positivity (E009), leading to the definitive diagnosis of sinonasal teratocarcinosarcoma. A postoperative PET scan showed ongoing soft tissue thickening in the left nasal cavity and sinuses but no evidence of distal FDG-avid disease (E005).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with nasal obstruction, intermittent epistaxis, and anosmia, and a large tissue growth in the left nasal cavity.
CT scan revealed a large soft tissue mass opacifying the left maxillary, ethmoidal, frontal, and sphenoid sinuses, without intracranial extension.

Formal examination of the whole specimen, including immunohistochemistry, showed a heterogeneous mixture of components from all three germ cell layers (mature benign glandular/stromal, immature malignant glandular/stromal), with undifferentiated components showing CD-99 or synaptophysin positivity, consistent with sinonasal teratocarcinosarcoma.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: This was a provisional diagnosis on frozen section (E004) but was superseded by the comprehensive histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis of the whole specimen (E009) which revealed the complex, multi-germ layer nature characteristic of teratocarcinosarcoma.
